haiku-low.q1: Step 4, after build and lint, before any new instance starts; the currently live release must keep working against the migrated schema.
haiku-low.q2: Only in a later release, after the release still using the old column or table has been retired.
haiku-low.q3: Every instance passes /healthz three times running and smoke tests pass within 10 minutes. Otherwise abort without touching the public listener.
haiku-low.q4: Repoint the public listener from the old target group to the new one in one step, no gradual shift.
haiku-low.q5: 5xx above 1% in any 5-minute window during the 15-minute watch. Rollback repoints listener to old colour; migrations and failed colour stay.
haiku-low.q6: 30 minutes after the switch. After the old colour is shut down, a rollback is a normal deploy of the previous release.
haiku-low.q7: NOT STATED for database state. The deploy stops, the new release is never started, and the live colour keeps serving.
haiku-low.q8: The public listener's target is the source of truth: the colour it forwards to is live; the other is idle.
haiku-low.q9: Lock held by CI group catalog-web-deploy; others queue. Held from step 1 until step 10 release, or freed by CI if job dies.
haiku-low.q10: Internal-only test listener on the same load balancer points at idle colour's target group; users cannot reach it.
haiku-low.q11: The CI pipeline, at step 4 'Run migrations, once', before any new instance starts. The mechanism ensuring a single run is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q12: After abort, new instances are shut down. After rollback, the failed colour keeps running and the next deploy replaces it.

sonnet.q1: Step 4, after build/lint and before any new-release instance starts. The release currently serving traffic (the old/live release) must keep working, since migrations are additive.
sonnet.q2: Only in a later release, after the release that still uses the old column/table has been retired. The migration lint rejects drops/renames in a deploy.
sonnet.q3: Every instance must pass /healthz three times in a row (10s apart), then the smoke test suite must pass via the test listener, all within 10 minutes of instances starting. If not: abort without touching the public listener, shut down the new instances, migrations stay, lock released, engineers alerted.
sonnet.q4: In one step (step 7): the public listener is repointed from the old target group to the new one. No gradual shift.
sonnet.q5: Trigger: new colour's 5xx rate above 1% in any 5-minute window during the 15-minute watch (an engineer can also start a manual rollback job). A rollback repoints the public listener back to the old colour; it never reverses migrations. The failed new colour is left running for investigation, and the deploy ends at step 10 without tearing anything down.
sonnet.q6: 30 minutes after the switch (old colour kept running). After the old colour is shut down, a problem is handled by a normal deploy of the previous release.
sonnet.q7: NOT STATED for the database state left by a partial migration. The deploy stops, the new release is never started, the live colour keeps serving, the lock is released and engineers are alerted.
sonnet.q8: Read the public listener's target (step 2): that colour is live, the other is idle and receives the new release. The public listener's target is the source of truth for which colour is live (release per colour is in a release tag on instances).
sonnet.q9: The deploy lock, a CI concurrency group named catalog-web-deploy; later runs wait in the queue. It is held from step 1 until step 10 (about 30+ minutes after the switch), except that a manual rollback job does not wait for it.
sonnet.q10: Through the test listener, an internal-only listener on the same load balancer, which the pipeline points at the idle colour's target group.
sonnet.q11: The CI pipeline runs them (step 4), once, applied to the shared database before any new-release instance starts. NOT STATED beyond that for a specific mechanism guaranteeing once-only; the deploy lock allows only one run at a time and the step runs once in sequence.
sonnet.q12: After an abort at step 6, the new instances are shut down. After a rollback, the failed new colour is left running for investigation, and the next deploy replaces it (it becomes the idle colour, since the listener points back at the old colour).
